claims.text: The CFO and COO must decide how to handle the customer contract in the asset purchase.
Asset closing is planned for 1 October; customer consent is outstanding and there is no reliable completion date.
Written customer consent and signed novation are required before contract transfer; novation replaces the seller with the buyer.
Closing on 1 October leaves the contract and service with the seller for up to 30 days at an agreed £18,000 fee paid by the buyer.
Deferring closing until consent and novation are complete means no transition fee but uncertain closing timing; the seller serves the customer until then.
Under both options, the seller remains the contracting party and liable to the customer until novation takes effect.
The team must choose between paying £18,000 to preserve the planned asset closing and deferring closing without a transition fee; counsel recommends neither.
